source.authors: Aoki N, Cui S, Ito C, Kumaishi K, Kobori S, Ichihashi Y, Yoshida S
source.title: Phenolic signals for prehaustorium formation in Striga hermonthica

value: syringic acid (SyA) at 5 µM induced prehaustoria in 100% of germinated seedlings, and acetosyringone (AS) induced approximately 80% at 20 µM
method: germinated seedlings exposed to the host-derived phenolic haustorium-inducing factors SyA and AS in 96-well plates; prehaustorium formation (swollen root tip with haustorial hairs) counted under a stereomicroscope
conditions: Seeds preconditioned 1 week at 25 C in the dark, then germinated with 10 nM (+)-strigol for 24 h at 25 C in the dark; germinated seedlings placed in 96-well plates (100 µl per well, approximately 20 to 40 seedlings per well) with the compound and kept 24 h at 25 C in the dark; induction rate = seedlings with prehaustorium / total seedlings per well; three wells as three replicates; the Methods name no statistical test for these percentages. The text gives no concentration series for the kinetic assay in the Methods, and the Figure 1 legend lists SyA at 20 µM (with DMBQ 10 µM and AS 50 µM) for its single 24 h comparison, whereas the sentence quoted gives SyA at 5 µM, so the concentration for the 100% value rests on the sentence. The preceding sentence says induction rose linearly with concentration for all compounds, and the next says DMBQ was more active than the phenolics (consistent with Wada et al. 2019). DMSO solvent control: no inhibitory effect at the highest concentration (Supplemental Figure 1); no untreated or water-control induction rate is stated in the text read. SyA and AS are phenolics applied as chemicals; the text says they were previously reported as haustorium-inducing in P. japonicum and S. hermonthica.
where: Results, first paragraph (second sentence after the Figure 1C kinetics sentence)
quote: Whereas SyA induced prehaustorium in 100% of S. hermonthica seedlings at 5 µM, AS exhibited approximately 80% at even 20 µM, illustrating the higher potency of SyA compared to AS.
note: Prehaustorium (haustorium initiation) in the living root parasite in response to host-derived phenolic signals. SyA and AS are defined in the preceding sentence (the value spells them out). WFO: list.worldfloraonline.org/wfo-0000496049 (opened; page of the synonym Striga campuleia, states Striga hermonthica accepted, id wfo-0001138081, December 2023 snapshot); POWO: powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:810025-1 (opened) Striga hermonthica (Delile) Benth. 'This species is accepted'. Crossref checked (7 authors in printed order, vol 13, article 1077996, CC BY). source.authors: Krupp A, Bertsch B, Spring O
source.title: Costunolide Influences Germ Tube Orientation in Sunflower Broomrape – A First Step Toward Understanding Chemotropism

value: 76 ± 17% of germ tubes grew toward costunolide (10-4 M on the filter paper) within 2 mm of the source, against 48 ± 11% positive in the outer zone (2-5 mm)
method: Petri-dish chemotropism bioassay: germinated seeds in a ring around a filter-paper source of costunolide; germ tubes bending toward the source scored positive, away negative, no clear direction indeterminable
conditions: Seeds of O. cumana pathotype G (collected in the Rostov region of Russia in 2012) conditioned at least 1 week at 18 C in darkness on moist filter discs; dishes sealed and kept in the dark at 18 C; seeds placed with the micropyle alternately left and right in a concentric circle, 2 mm from the filter; seeds per dish not stated. Costunolide (a sesquiterpene lactone of sunflower) purchased from Selleck Chemicals, dissolved and diluted in methanol; 23 ppm = 10-4 M. Figure 4: n = 5-7 replications, mean ± SD, Tukey test p < 0.05; the legend says germ tubes closer to the source showed significantly higher chemotropism percentages toward costunolide but not toward GR24; the text does not say whether the 48% outer-zone value differs from an even split. The synthetic strigolactone GR24 (1 ppm = 3.3 x 10-6 M) gave no significant difference between positive and negative bending at either distance, with germ tubes curving toward and away in equal ratio; GR24 still induced germination. No methanol-only control result is reported in the text read. Sunflower root exudate and sunflower oil extract also gave around 70% positive reactions (Figure 3, n = 3-19 biological experiments), but that sentence is over 40 words and pools an extract, so it is not logged.
quote: Within a distance of 2 mm, 76 ± 17% of the germ tubes grew toward costunolide (10−4 M applied on the filter paper), while in the outer zone (2–5 mm), only 48 ± 11% showed positive chemotropism (Figure 4).
note: Directed growth (chemotropism) of the living parasite's germ tube toward a host-derived compound; the costunolide used was purchased pure, not a sunflower preparation. 'This species is accepted'. Crossref checked (3 authors in printed order, vol 12, article 699068, CC BY 4.0). source.authors: Irafasha G, Mutinda S, Mobegi F, Hale B, Omwenga G, Wijeratne AJ, Wicke S, Bellis ES, Runo S
source.title: Transcriptome atlas of Striga germination: Implications for managing an intractable parasitic plant

value: at 18 h after induction, 49.79% of seeds germinated with root exudate of sorghum line IS2730, not different from 45.76% with GR24, and higher than 20.50% (IS27146), 24.90% (SRN39) and 20.05% (IS41724)
method: germination of conditioned seeds induced with sorghum root exudate (four lines) or GR24, scored as percentage germinated at 6, 12 and 18 h after induction
conditions: Seeds collected in 2018 from infested fields in Alupe, Kenya; conditioned seeds given 1 ml root exudate per gram root weight, or 5 ml GR24 at 0.1 ppm as positive control, in sealed foil-covered Petri plates incubated in the dark at 30 C for 24 h; exudate from hydroponically grown sorghum seedlings (Long Ashton medium, then 48 h in sterile distilled water); conditioned untreated seeds were the negative control and no germination percentage for them is given in the text read; five technical and three biological replicates in a completely randomized design; Tukey HSD at 5%, Figure 1 legend 'p < .05; n = 15' (letters shown for treatments at the same time point); the text gives no test statistic for these percentages, and the number of seeds per dish is not stated. Earlier times: at 6 h germination occurred with IS2730 (16.45%), GR24 (15.62%) and IS27146 (15.36%) but not with SRN39 or IS41724; at 12 h all treatments germinated (GR24 24.61%, IS2730 22.49%, IS27146 18.83%, IS41724 17.32%, SRN39 20.48%).
quote: Overall, there were no difference in seeds treated with IS2730 (49.79%) and GR24 (45.76%), but these values were higher than IS27146 (20.50%), SRN39 (24.90%), and IS41724 (20.05%) observed at that time point.
note: Germination of the living parasite's seeds in response to host (sorghum) root exudate; the paper's main aim is a transcriptome of germination, and GR24 appears as a comparator, not as the signal logged. 'hai' = hours after induction. Printed in Plants, People, Planet 7(2) (2025); Crossref gives an issued year of 2023 (online) for the same volume and pages.
